rv.q: Fortunately, the veteran performer is an utterly engaging storyteller, delivering her bleak but ultimately empowering tale with a skilfully judged balance of dignity, self-deprecating humour and controlled fury.
So much here is shocking, tragic and incendiary but it is not given enough oxygen to unleash its terrible power.
Lahti delivers a performance that holds our attention, captures our hearts, and shines a light on the secrets that lie beneath the ostensibly perfect family.
Indeed, walking that line is the show’s biggest challenge.
The Smile of Her is a remarkable piece of theatre—intelligent, emotionally generous and quietly unforgettable.
The Smile of Her is a deeply personal piece of theatre that will stay with audiences long after they leave the theatre.
It is a quietly healing experience, one that feels less like watching a play and more like sharing in an intensely personal act of reflection.
She has masterfully crafted her experience into a compelling journey of self-discovery and reflection, delivering her story with warmth and vulnerability.
This is a homage to all women — their growth, the price they pay for their audacity to demand better, their refusal to be broken, smile or not.
Overall, The Smile of Her has many aspects to praise, from its honesty to its design and acting performances.
I cannot hide how disappointing this show was. When someone is telling their own lived truth on stage, you expect a profound sense of honesty, but this missed that vital spark.
She is a vivid storyteller over seven life changing decades.
The Smile of Her is an engaging and heartfelt autobiographical portrait that demonstrates the power of simple storytelling.

cn.t: Lahti's autobiographical solo show earns praise for her engaging storytelling and brave exploration of family trauma and misogyny, though some critics find it overstuffed with too many themes crammed into 90 minutes.
